purpose: design how the system uses cloud services so it is secure, resilient across failures, cost-aware and operable from code
entry_criteria: Requirements, quality targets and data classification exist
A cloud provider and account strategy is chosen
procedure: Design the account or subscription structure: separate environments and workloads, central logging and guardrails with organization-level policies.
Design networking: private subnets for workloads, controlled ingress and egress, private connectivity to managed services and segmentation by trust.
Design resilience to the failure level required: multi-zone by default, and multi-region only where the recovery objectives justify the cost and complexity.
Choose managed services where they reduce operational load, noting lock-in, limits and failure modes of each.
Design identity: roles with least privilege, no long-lived keys, and separate admin paths with strong authentication.
Define everything as code with environments created from the same definitions, and estimate the run cost with the assumptions.
deliverables: infrastructure as code layout and cost estimate
acceptance_criteria: Resilience level matches the recovery objectives
Workloads sit in private networks with controlled egress

validation.command: terraform validate && terraform plan -out=plan.out   # example; use the project's IaC tool

validation.check: map each recovery objective to the design element that meets it

failure_modes.response: Use private subnets and explicit ingress

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A service runs across three zones in one region because the recovery objective is a 30-minute RTO for zone loss; workloads are in private subnets, access uses roles, and the whole stack is created from code.
